Abstract: This chapter reviews recent advances in elucidating autophagy. Although autophagosomes are known to be the sole source of cytosolic proteins for autophagosome maturation, they can also be considered to be lysosomes and therefore termed lysosome associated organelles. The concept of autophagosome was introduced as a general model of the degradation pathway. The autophagosome is an intermediate step that initiates autophagosome maturation. Recent advances in understanding autophagy in the cells have not only highlighted the concept of autophagosomes but also revealed the cellular mechanisms involved in the autophagic process. In this chapter, the roles of autophagy in normal cells and cancer cells are reviewed.

The framework includes the possibility for more specific choices of node and link probabilities and their combinations. This allows the modelling of networks containing complex interactions.
